To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the acoustic emission characteristics of electrical tree growth in a plastic resin are different depending upon the type of tree and that void formation is accompanied by the largest AE signals.
the AE distribution is different between the different types of electrical tree growth and void formation.
the amplitude of acoustic emissions (AE) from branch-like and filamentic trees is relatively small, and that the AE amplitude distribution exhibited a narrow peak at small amplitudes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
AE characteristics during electrical tree growth in a polyester resin.
the relationship between the types of tree and AE characteristics.
the acoustic emission characteristics of electrical treeing in polyethylene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AE characteristics depend on the types of tree and on the formation of voids.
AE activity was related to the growth and formation of void in the tree, and that the AE activity was related with the growth and formation process of the electrical tree.
AE from branch-like and filamenty trees is associated with tree growth and propagation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AE activity is closely related to tree activity, especially to the growth of the tree branches, but the AE activity at void formation is not directly related to tree growth.
AE signals are related to the growth of the tree branches, the growth of the voids and the growth of the filamentary tree.
the AE amplitude and distribution are useful to characterize the types of trees and voids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AE is useful in monitoring electrical tree growth and void formation in plastic insulating materials.
the acoustic emission (AE) signal from the electrical tree is a useful tool in the analysis of tree growth.
the AE characteristics are different for each type of tree, and the AE characteristics change with time during tree growth.
